name: Three Federal Laws in Plain English
title: Three Federal Laws in Plain English
answer: Three federal laws carry most of the load when schools protect students online: FERPA covers education records, COPPA covers the personal information of children under 13 on commercial sites and apps, and CIPA sets filtering and safety rules for schools that take federal internet discounts. A fourth law, the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, gives parents rights over surveys and marketing aimed at their children and can matter when an AI tool asks about sensitive topics. Knowing which law applies to which situation is what lets a school adopt AI tools without guessing at its obligations.

crumbs.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule

sections.body: This idea is a plain English map of the federal laws that govern student privacy and safety online, so that school decisions about AI tools start from the right legal frame rather than from vendor claims. FERPA protects student education records, COPPA protects the personal information of children under 13 when they use commercial websites and apps, and CIPA sets internet filtering and safety rules for schools that receive federal discounts for internet service. A fourth law, the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, gives parents rights over surveys and marketing involving their children. It matters less for most AI tools, but it can apply when a tool asks students about sensitive topics. The problem it solves is confusion: without this map, a school may apply the wrong law to a tool, or assume no law applies at all.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a school uses this map to sort each AI tool by what it actually does. If a tool touches student education records, FERPA is the frame. If it collects personal information from children under 13 through a commercial website or app, COPPA is the frame. If the question is about filtering and safety on school internet service that receives federal discounts, CIPA is the frame. When a tool asks students about sensitive topics, the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment can come into play because of the rights it gives parents over surveys and marketing. The text presents the four laws side by side in Figure 3.2 and then examines each one more closely, with attention to how AI changes what each law asks of a school. The text does not give grade band examples for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or finding for this idea beyond the statement that Figure 3.2 sets the four laws side by side. It offers no evidence label and no research result. This idea therefore rests on practice and on the plain text of the laws as the book describes them, rather than on research evidence.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits here are about scope and fit. The Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment matters less for most AI tools, but it can apply when a tool asks students about sensitive topics, so a school cannot dismiss it outright. Each law is described as doing part of the work, which means no single law covers every situation a school will meet. The decisions about which law applies to a given tool, and what the school will do about it, stay with the people responsible for the school's choices. This page describes practice and is not legal advice.
